Law III The Leap from Quantity to Quality
Development is not a simple circle of gradual growth. Imperceptible quantitative
changes accumulate and trigger rapid, fundamental qualitative changes.
Steam (Qualitative Leap)
Heating Water (Quantitative Change)

Application to Social Policy:
Reforms (quantitative change)
cannot liberate the working
class. Transition requires a
qualitative leap: Revolution.

Law IV | The Struggle of Opposites
Internal contradictions are inherent in all things. Everything contains a
past and a future, a negative and a positive.
"Development is the 'struggle of opposites."
- Lenin
The internal content of all transformation is the collision of these opposed forces.
Therefore, the class struggle is a natural, inevitable phenomenon.

The Insurmountable
Obstacle
Spontaneous Growth
Blind, unconscious evolution. Early
bourgeoisie invented manufactories
simply to make profit, unwittingly
destroying feudalism.
Conscious Revolution
Once new productive forces mature, the
ruling classes become an insuperable
obstacle defending old property relations.
Spontaneous development must yield to
conscious, unified political action.
"Force is the midwife of every old society
pregnant with a new one."
_ Karl Marx

The Inevitable Arc of History
Dialectics: Nature is driven by inherent
contradictions and rapid qualitative leaps.
Materialism: Human consciousness and ideas are
merely a reflection of physical material reality.
Historical Materialism: Material reality is relentlessly
pushed forward by the expanding forces of production.
Mankind only sets itself tasks it can solve. The conflict between modern
productive forces and capitalist relations of production guarantees that an
epoch of social revolution is a scientific inevitability.
